technology.title: QWC mainnet combines RandomX mining with EPoSe service rewards.
technology.body: Qwertycoin is a new mainnet chain derived from the Monero v0.18.5.1 codebase, with QWC parameters, HF17-era privacy technology, RandomX proof of work, and EPoSe from genesis.

features.title: QWC Core Network
features.body: The current QWC chain is mainnet. Active operators, miners, and Service Nodes are hardening the live network.

features.title: Modern privacy base
features.body: QWC starts from Monero v0.18.5.1 with HF17-era privacy technology and QWC-specific parameters from genesis.

features.title: RandomX proof of work
features.body: RandomX miners produce blocks, secure ordering, and keep chain security separate from service-node reward eligibility.

features.title: Proof of Service rewards
features.body: Registered Service Nodes prove useful network service through deterministic attestations before they can enter reward rotation.

features.title: Service Nodes are not validators
features.body: Service Nodes do not lock stake, produce blocks, or vote on chain history. RandomX proof of work remains responsible for consensus ordering.

features.title: Wallet and source available
features.body: The website, web wallet beta, and public QWC core source are available. Signed binaries and broader tooling follow in staged releases.

epose.title: RandomX PoW secures the blockchain. EPoSe rewards decentralized network service.
epose.body: No central Sentinel decides which Service Nodes receive rewards. Chain state and EPoSe rules determine qualification, payee selection, and reward validity.
epose.intro: QWC divides service time into EPoSe epochs. Service activity produces attestations, qualification is finalized, and only then can deterministic reward rotation use the qualified set.

compactCards.title: Service activity
compactCards.body: Registered Service Nodes provide useful QWC network service during each epoch.

compactCards.title: Attestations
compactCards.body: Deterministically assigned verifier committees check service activity and create signed attestations.

compactCards.title: Reward rotation
compactCards.body: Qualification is finalized before deterministic payee selection can affect service rewards.

epose.originBody: The original EPoSe vision and Qwertycoin service-layer whitepaper work came from Xecute, a historical honorary member of the Qwertycoin project. QWC finally carries that plan forward as a decentralized chain-state implementation.

steps.title: Register
steps.body: A Service Node publishes a signed registration with service identity, reward target, endpoint commitment, and admission proof.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: The node provides QWC network service while normal RandomX mining remains responsible for block production.

steps.title: Attest
steps.body: Assigned verifiers challenge the Service Node and sign attestations only when the expected service response is valid.

steps.title: Qualify
steps.body: Chain state determines whether a registered node collected enough valid attestations for the relevant epoch.

steps.title: Reward
steps.body: Qualified nodes enter deterministic reward rotation. One selected payee can receive the EPoSe part of a block reward.

glossary.definition: A normal QWC node plus a registered service identity, endpoint commitment, reward address, and EPoSe participation data.
A fixed block period in which service activity is measured. Current parameter: {blocks} blocks, roughly {hours} hours at a {seconds} second block target.
The Service Node joined EPoSe by publishing a valid on-chain registration. Registered does not mean reward-eligible.
A signed confirmation from an assigned verifier that the Service Node answered its service challenge with the expected response.
A deterministic set of verifier nodes selected from chain state for a service challenge. It checks service activity only; it does not produce blocks.
A small proof attached to registration that makes identities cost work to create and helps reduce cheap Sybil registrations.
A registered Service Node that collected enough valid, non-duplicate attestations during the relevant epoch.
The finalized epoch whose qualified set is used for the current reward period. In the current core, blocks in epoch N use qualified nodes from epoch N-1.
Qualified nodes are deterministically rotated as possible recipients of the EPoSe part of block rewards. The coinbase does not grow with the total node count.

epose.epochTitle: Epochs are block ranges, not clock appointments.
epose.epochBody: An EPoSe epoch is a {blocks}-block service period, roughly {hours} hours at the current {seconds}-second block target.

registeredVsQualified.label: Qualified
registeredVsQualified.body: The node proved enough service activity to become eligible for service rewards.

epose.committeeTitle: Verifier committees are not validator sets.
epose.committeeBody: Verifier committees do not produce blocks and do not replace RandomX miners. Their role is limited to checking Service Node activity for EPoSe qualification. Self-attestations do not qualify a node, and duplicate votes from the same verifier for the same subject and epoch are rejected by consensus state.
epose.rewardTimelineTitle: Service is measured first. Rewards follow later.

timeline.label: Epoch N
timeline.title: Register / Serve / Attest
timeline.body: Service Nodes register, provide service, and collect valid verifier attestations.

timeline.label: Finality
timeline.title: Qualification finalized
timeline.body: Consensus state derives the qualified set from valid EPoSe data after the epoch is final.

timeline.label: Epoch N+1
timeline.title: Reward rotation
timeline.body: The current core uses the previous epoch as the reward source epoch for deterministic payee selection.

epose.rotationTitle: Reward rotation keeps block rewards compact.
epose.rotationBody: Current mainnet reward split: 90% miner / {rewardPercent}% EPoSe service reward. EPoSe service payouts are consensus-visible so every node can verify the selected Service Node and reward amount. Normal QWC wallet transactions continue to use the privacy mechanisms of the underlying QWC transaction model.
epose.sentinelBody: Explorer and Sentinel-style tooling can observe and monitor, but consensus derives EPoSe state from the chain. Current mainnet reward split: 90% miner / {rewardPercent}% EPoSe service reward.

items.question: Does EPoSe replace mining?
items.answer: No. RandomX miners still produce blocks and secure the chain. EPoSe adds a service-reward layer for registered infrastructure.

items.question: What is an epoch?
items.answer: An epoch is a fixed block period used by EPoSe to measure and finalize service activity. The current QWC parameter is {blocks} blocks, roughly {hours} hours.

items.question: What does qualified mean?
items.answer: Qualified means a registered Service Node has enough valid attestations in the relevant epoch to become reward-eligible.

items.question: Who decides whether a Service Node is qualified?
items.answer: No central server. Qualification is derived deterministically from QWC chain state and valid EPoSe registration and attestation data.

items.question: Do Service Nodes need to stake QWC?
items.answer: No QWC staking role is defined in the current EPoSe core. Service Nodes register a service identity and admission proof; they are not proof-of-stake validators.

items.question: Can one operator run multiple Service Nodes?
items.answer: The protocol can represent multiple Service Node identities. Admission proof makes cheap identity creation harder, but it is not a promise that one human equals one node.

items.question: Why is EPoSe not Proof of Stake?
items.answer: Service Nodes do not lock stake, produce blocks, or vote on chain history. RandomX proof of work remains responsible for block production and ordering.

serviceNodes.title: Run infrastructure. Prove service. Earn QWC.
serviceNodes.body: A normal node validates, syncs, and relays. A Service Node adds a registered identity, public service commitment, proof/attestation flow, qualification, and reward eligibility.
rows: Synchronizes the blockchain, validates blocks, relays transactions, and contributes peer capacity.
Does everything a normal node does, plus registers a service identity and participates in the EPoSe service-reward protocol.
No reward path beyond mining if the operator also mines blocks.
Can become qualified for deterministic service rewards after registration and attestations.
Also not a proof-of-stake validator. RandomX miners still produce blocks.

mining.title: RandomX, not CryptoNight.
mining.body: Old CryptoNight and old mining pool instructions are legacy material. QWC uses RandomX proof of work with a 120 second block target.

cards.title: Permissionless PoW
cards.body: Mining is open to anyone who can run compatible RandomX mining software against a QWC node or pool. Active pool documentation will be linked only after it is verified for v2.

cards.title: No validator council
cards.body: QWC is not proof of stake. Service Nodes receive service rewards only through the EPoSe layer; they do not replace proof-of-work block production.

wallet.title: Wallet - beta and planned releases
wallet.body: QWC mainnet is live. Wallet products are separate rollout items: the web wallet is in beta, PWA installation is in development, and the desktop GUI is planned.

cards.title: Web Wallet
cards.body: The non-custodial browser wallet beta is available at wallet.qwertycoin.org for the current QWC mainnet. Early beta - use with care.

cards.title: PWA
cards.body: Installable PWA behavior is in development and should not be presented as a finished release yet.

cards.title: Desktop GUI
cards.body: A modern desktop GUI wallet is planned after the web wallet engine and QWC transaction path are hardened.

releases.title: Qwertycoin Releases
releases.body: Mainnet release communication is staged: website first, web wallet beta next, public QWC source after that, then broader wallet and ecosystem tooling.

cards.title: Web Wallet

cards.title: Desktop GUI

cards.title: Public QWC Source

cards.title: Additional Wallets & Tools

history.title: 2018 roots. 2026 QWC Mainnet.
history.body: The legacy Qwertycoin ecosystem matters, but it must not be confused with Qwertycoin.

items.title: Qwertycoin launches
items.body: QWC began as a CryptoNote-based community privacy coin with early wallet, explorer, community, and infrastructure efforts.

items.title: EPoW and EPoSe experiments
items.body: The project explored fair mining, service rewards, wallets, nodes, infrastructure, and voting concepts. Xecute's EPoSe work remains part of that origin story.

items.title: Stagnation and token phase
items.body: The legacy chain and ecosystem diverged from what QWC needs today. Exchange, price, wallet, and old source claims from that era are not reused as current facts.

items.title: Qwertycoin Mainnet
items.body: Qwertycoin returns as a new mainnet chain with RandomX, modern privacy technology, QWC HF17 rules, and EPoSe v2.

history.alert: Qwertycoin is a new mainnet chain. Old chain data, wallet cache files, peer state, and old release binaries are not compatible with this network.

developers.title: Build and review the public QWC source.
developers.body: The current QWC v2 core source is public. Release binaries, checksums, and operator guidance continue through controlled release gates.
developers.sourceBody: The current core source is available in qwertycoin-org/qwertycoin. Review the repository and its build notes before running mainnet software.
developers.legacyBody: Older public repositories may remain available for history, but they must not be treated as the current QWC core source.
developers.registrationBody: Service-node registration, attestation, qualification, and reward tooling is developed alongside the public QWC core source and remains subject to release review.

community.title: Open source, careful by default.
community.body: Only active and controlled resources are linked from this mainnet website. Legacy docs and old wallet/download/exchange links remain excluded until they are updated or clearly archived.

footer.body: Qwertycoin mainnet, wallet beta, and public source are live. Additional ecosystem releases continue in controlled stages.
